title: How John Rush runs 24 products: niche-first, no-ask feedback, build in public, buying back time
summary: John Rush explains how he left VC-backed startups for bootstrapping 24 products and grew on X from 72 followers. He covers niche-first strategy, never asking for feedback, turning his own problems into products, and buying back time with tools.

principles.text: Go as narrow as you can on niche. Broad markets are a lottery crowded with funded competitors. Widen later by removing filters.
principles.quote: I think the more Niche you go the better and you have to cut it from all the sides you can it has to be you know one problem one specific type of problem within that problem

principles.text: Never ask for feedback. Open a channel so users volunteer it, e.g. invite-only signup via DMs.
principles.quote: I never ask for feedback not a single time in my life like never and the thing I do instead is that I create a Channel between us so that you feel comfortable asking not asking but giving the feedback

principles.text: Feedback from free users, friends, or people you ask is unreliable. Trust unprompted feedback from people far from you.
principles.quote: feedback from free users is bad for you feedback from friends is bad for you and feedback from people who you ask for feedback is also bad

principles.text: Grow on X by copying what big accounts did early, then become yourself and post what your ideal followers would post.
principles.quote: I just look at people with a lot of followers I scrolled far back to their Old Post and there's filter on Twitter you can do that

principles.text: Your own problems are your best product ideas. Run tools internally first, and productize what costs you 10 hours a month.
principles.quote: my problem is my fuel and the way I come up with all the ideas if there was no problem my ideas would would be worthless because I would be just guessing what people need

principles.text: Buy back your time with paid tools rather than doing things by hand. Hours saved outweigh $100/month.
principles.quote: almost everything you do could be bought back if you pay something and you save time right
